implementation_notes: C provides no serialization, delegation or versioning machinery, so the window is a translation unit that keeps the legacy header byte-for-byte - prototypes, struct layouts, enum widths and error codes - and puts an opaque handle in front of the new core, leaving the (de)marshalling to be written by hand. The discipline that makes this viable is the one libcurl documents for its own C interface: a library upgrade must not break the ABI, and an interface break is admitted only through a deliberate SONAME bump so old binaries keep working. The hand-written form is still justified whenever the legacy consumer was compiled against the old header or is a binary that cannot be re-linked; where the consumer can be rebuilt, generate both sides from one schema instead.
pitfalls: Struct layout is part of the contract: reordering fields, inserting one in the middle, or letting padding and alignment drift breaks binary consumers even though the source still compiles.

Ownership of returned data must match the old convention exactly (caller-provided buffer, library-owned pointer, or free-with-library-function); mixing them corrupts the heap of a process you do not control.
Old error conventions are shape too: errno side effects, short returns and partial-success codes are what the calling code actually tests.
